correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite graphs, a nonempty selected set dominates iff it meets two classes or fills one class; its complement has no isolate iff empty or meeting two classes. For p=0 every singleton qualifies when N≥3, and the two blocks in K₂ form a coalition. For p≥2, singleton-class vertices qualify by themselves; vertices in large classes can pair across two large classes, leaving members of both classes outside. This proves the maximum N in both cases. With one large class and u=1, the only restrained dominating set is all vertices, hence the maximum is two. When u≥2 each clique vertex is itself restrained dominating, and splitting the large class into two proper nonempty blocks gives the asserted u+2. Theorem 2.1 of Dobrynin–Glebov–Golmohammadi supplies the upper bound by the ordinary coalition number: every block containing a universal vertex must be its singleton in an ordinary coalition partition, and the large class can contribute at most two blocks, since a pair of its blocks dominates only if it covers that whole class. Independently, if three or more blocks lie entirely within the large class, a union of two such blocks cannot dominate, and a potential partner containing a clique vertex either is already RD (another clique vertex and a large-class vertex remain outside) or contains all clique vertices and its union still leaves an independent outside. This also excludes more than u+2 blocks directly. It gives 4 for K_{3,1,1}. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; it visits all 101632 candidate partitions on 58 profiles through order 8, with validity tests pruned by the incumbent order. The proof, not enumeration, covers all orders.
